review_role: Author proposals independently reviewed; main integrated bounded wording, selection and origin deltas. Offline candidates only; original banks and holds unchanged.
comparison_universe: The existing chapter 62-64 entries, their named older prior records and saved attempts; targeted term matches and selected cue-ingredient matches in chapter audit JSON files numbered below 62, plus the canonical phonetic-lens record. This was not an exhaustive semantic, alias, workshop, external-mnemonic or corpus-wide originality audit. No new source extraction, internet, provider calls or renders.
classification_basis: Novelty is relative to named comparisons, not this session or corpus-wide uniqueness. Selection and change_origin are separate axes. Existing candidate recounts are not newly added associations. Supplemental candidates do not resolve canonical holds or enter production.
limits: Editorial language/image judgments only. No clinical assertions, source completeness, empirical pronunciation, object naming, learner recall, render quality or exhaustive novelty claims. A supplemental selection does not resolve a canonical hold. Historical decisions remain untouched.

entries.proposed_cue: An ordinary toy tree alone, without catheter; keep the existing proposal.
entries.encoded_scope: Approximate tre-/tree name fragment only; no breathing or positional content.
entries.why: The older Aintree catheter record actually pairs a toy tree with a detached hollow catheter. Tree already supplies a tree-name fragment there. Removing the device and assigning the same tree fragment to another word is useful reuse, but not enough to establish a different bridge. No extra prop is needed merely to claim yield.
entries.limitations: Tre-/tree compression and collision with other tree-name fragments require teaching. The original target has changed, but substantially the same partial-sound strategy remains.

entries.proposed_cue: A plain memorial gravestone alone; keep the existing partial-name proposal.
entries.encoded_scope: Grav-/grave sound reminder within gravis only; myasthenia and condition identity unencoded.
entries.why: The actual older cue is a memorial gravestone beside a patient-name card, using the memorial/death category. The chapter 62 bridge instead uses grave as a name sound. That semantic-to-phonetic reassignment is a distinct useful association despite the old prop. Chapter 29A also has an unresolved same-term hold; this supplement does not erase it. Already present in chapter 62, not an additional invention in this review.
entries.limitations: The death-category baggage is a real collision risk; the cue must not imply mortality or prognosis. Partial-name recovery is untested.

entries.proposed_cue: An ordinary bar of soap alone, without factory or bubbles; keep the existing proposal.
entries.encoded_scope: Bar/Barré approximate partial-name reminder only; Guillain and syndrome identity omitted.
entries.why: The actual metabolic alkalosis cue combines a factory/conveyor and soap/bubbles, using a learned soap/base category. Here the object's ordinary name bar supplies the sound bridge. This is not simply another alkalosis scene or a claim that soap is a novel object. Already present in chapter 62.
entries.limitations: Barré pronunciation and naming the object soap rather than bar may weaken recovery. No drug, chemistry, cause or syndrome meaning is inferred.

entries.proposed_cue: An ordinary marker pen beside a broad soft-edged ink patch on paper; retain the declared chapter 62 addition.
entries.encoded_scope: Diffuse/soft-edged everyday appearance only; impairment and physiological meaning unencoded.
entries.why: The actual older cue is a heart token beside a marker pen: marker is the lexical bridge. It does not contain the soft-edged ink patch. Chapter 62 explicitly adds that appearance and uses diffuse rather than marker as the bridge. Both the changed association and the added visual state deserve recognition; no new root object is required. Already present in chapter 62.
entries.limitations: A static patch may read as a stain rather than diffusion. No gas exchange, impaired process or clinical explanation is depicted or validated.

entries.proposed_cue: A mannequin eye with a conspicuously cyan iris; keep the existing cyan-head cue without claiming a new bridge.
entries.encoded_scope: Cyan color/name head only; no cyanosis finding or cyanide identity.
entries.why: The actual cyanide record declares Cyan/eye name fragments, not cyan alone. Chapter62 reuses the identical cyan-iris eye but retains only the cyan fragment in its declared target scope. The retained cyan bridge and depiction are unchanged; dropping the eye fragment without changing the picture is not counted as a new association or substantive visual variant. The older cyanosis hold remains preserved.
entries.limitations: Strong cross-term collision is expected at this scope. Eye color must not be read as a diagnostic sign; the old hold is not resolved by this overlay.

entries.encoded_scope: No selected association. Reconsidered the saved colored-paint-swatch attempt and a prom/dance name fragment.
entries.why: The saved chlor/color compression remains weak for this author. A prom reminder could use an interior fragment, which is allowed, but a generic dance scene would not reliably supply prom rather than dance or party. No economical concrete revision selected. The actual older Gray record is a color-category host, not evidence that a Chlorpromazine bridge already existed.
entries.limitations: Editorial nonselection, not measured failure or an all-syllables veto. A familiar prom association for a particular learner could change the judgment; no such evidence was collected.

entries.encoded_scope: No selected association. Reconsidered shirt and a schist-rock naming route.
entries.why: The saved shirt attempt still requires a substantial schist/shirt sound repair. A rock taught as schist would improve the lexical fragment but an ordinary rock does not make that particular name economical here. No biological or disease-topic prop was substituted for a name bridge.
entries.limitations: Rock-subtype familiarity was not tested. This does not rule out a learned schist cue for an audience already familiar with that word, and does not require whole-name recovery.

entries.proposed_cue: A familiar taxi toy alone; remove the epic-story book from the held assembly.
entries.encoded_scope: Taxi/taxis approximate ending-name reminder only; epi- and clinical meaning unencoded.
entries.why: The saved chapter 63 attempt already contains a taxi beside an epic-story book. Selecting the taxi fragment alone removes the hard-to-see epic category and arbitrary two-prop assembly. This is a narrower, more economical variant of an actual held attempt, not a newly invented taxi association. The older Abciximab cue also uses a taxi, but for the different approximate cixi/ksi fragment. This is the newly selected supplemental candidate in this review.
entries.limitations: The missing final s and taxi-versus-cab naming are explicit sound risks. The fragment is not unique and does not encode nose, blood or any clinical state. Canonical chapter 63 hold stays unchanged pending independent review.

entries.proposed_cue: A familiar capped autoinjector training prop, taught as an epinephrine packaging/device association.
entries.encoded_scope: Taught epinephrine packaging/device association only; not unique drug identification, contents, injury or use.
entries.why: Main accepts the independent reviewer's broader category selection, disagreeing with the author's hold. The older chapter46 record encodes device category with drug identity explicitly omitted. This supplemental selection teaches a device-to-epinephrine association; that bridge differs from device category alone. It reconsiders an existing packaging route, not a newly invented prop, verified contents or a corpus-wide first association.
entries.limitations: Other drugs use autoinjectors. Context and teaching are required; no unique drug identity or empirical familiarity, recovery, safety, contents or technique claim. Original holds remain preserved. Author nonselection and reviewer/main disagreement are retained in the frozen author file and independent report.

entries.proposed_cue: A plain patch of grass alone; keep the existing pasture-category proposal without adding decorative props.
entries.encoded_scope: Pasture/grass learned landscape category within the name only; Good- and syndrome identity unencoded.
entries.why: The actual Nimodipine cue is a lawn mower mowing a grass patch, using mow/mo as an interior-name action. Chapter 63 removes the mower and recruits the grass patch for pasture, a different lexical/category bridge rather than another mow sound. The old ingredient family therefore understates association yield. Already present in chapter 63.
entries.limitations: A grass patch can be named lawn rather than pasture; the taught category bridge may be broad. No syndrome features, location or clinical claims follow from the landscape.

entries.encoded_scope: No selected association. Reconsidered the saved generic plant and an echo-based opening-name route.
entries.why: A generic potted plant remains topic-level rather than a helpful Echinacea-specific name/category reminder. Echo would require a less direct sound bridge plus a visual convention for repeated sound, so no concrete improvement selected. A specifically named plant could be a legitimate familiar category cue, but no saved identification evidence was consulted to specify one.
entries.limitations: No botanical identity, appearance, indication or effect is invented. This is not a rejection of all plant-category cues or of teaching a partial fragment.

entries.encoded_scope: No selected association. The existing toy-zither proposal remains a potentially teachable zith-/zither fragment, not a whole-name cue.
entries.why: The older chapter46 record already tried a toy zither and held it for instrument-name burden. Main retains the author's nonselection of this particular taught zither bridge; being old or lacking empirical familiarity evidence is not an admission veto. A generic guitar would lose the chosen zith-/zither name fragment. No alternative depiction is selected; the attempt remains eligible for future reconsideration.
entries.limitations: Instrument familiarity is uncertain, not empirically disproven. A learner who knows a zither may find this useful; no demand for all syllables or unique untrained naming is imposed. The historical hold stays open.

entries.proposed_cue: The old mannequin hand rapping its knuckles against a plain surface, without the sensory-mute icon; retain the chapter 64 added action.
entries.encoded_scope: Rap-/rapping ordinary action fragment only; remaining name and drug properties unencoded.
entries.why: The actual older numbness cue is a sensory-mute icon beside a mannequin hand; it contains no rapping action. A hand now performing rap supplies a different lexical bridge. Calling this only an old hand prop misses the new association and action already declared in chapter 64.
entries.limitations: A static image may read knock rather than rap; action naming and learned drug-name recovery are untested. No drug effect, route or sensory claim is represented.

entries.proposed_cue: A household-battery cell with an explicitly added cancellation slash; retain the chapter 64 negation variant.
entries.encoded_scope: A-/cell shared-word graphic only, contrasted with the existing whole cell battery cue; no biological composition assertion.
entries.why: The actual chapter 31 battery is an AAA acronym reminder, with no cancellation slash. Chapter 64 whole cell already uses the battery's ordinary cell name. Relative to that same-cell bridge, acellular adds a substantive visible negation and encoded scope; it is a meaningful variant, not another count for the battery alone. Already present in chapter 64. Earlier cancellation-slash grammar also exists elsewhere and is not claimed as new.
entries.limitations: The slash may read forbidden battery rather than a-/cell without teaching. The depicted battery is not a biological cell or a statement about a product's ingredients.

entries.proposed_cue: A detached camera lens; retain the existing partial-name proposal.
entries.encoded_scope: Lenz-/lens interior-name reminder only; re-, final vowel and medication properties unencoded.
entries.why: The actual canonical record has concept lens, objects detached camera lens and bridge lens -> lens; it does not encode Relenza. Chapter 64 applies that familiar object name to a different interior name fragment. This is a distinct name association relative to the literal lens headword, unlike merely reusing an already established cyan head. Already present in chapter 64, with no claim of corpus-wide first use.
entries.limitations: Lens/lenz sound tolerance and camera/zoom naming alternatives remain untested. This is not a medication identity test or an optical-effect claim.
